title: Filter routes before you optimize them
description: Choose a workload, trusted identity state, routing objective, and provider-health scenario. The lab first applies hard policy constraints, then ranks only the eligible routes.

identities.label: Verified workload identity
identities.detail: The gateway derives the tenant, plan, and data permissions from trusted authentication.

identities.label: Verified standard plan
identities.detail: The tenant is verified but its contract excludes restricted-data workloads.

identities.label: Valid identity, wrong tenant
identities.detail: The caller is authenticated, but the requested resource belongs to a different tenant.

identities.label: Client-supplied tenant header
identities.detail: The request claims a tenant without a trusted identity binding.

objectives.label: Balanced policy
objectives.detail: Prefer quality while preserving meaningful latency and cost headroom.

objectives.label: Quality-first policy
objectives.detail: Give measured task quality most of the ranking weight.

objectives.label: Cost-aware policy
objectives.detail: Prefer lower cost, but never override an eligibility rule.

healthScenarios.label: All routes healthy
healthScenarios.detail: Every route reports normal latency and a closed circuit.

healthScenarios.label: Fast route is slow
healthScenarios.detail: The normal low-latency route is degraded, but its circuit remains closed.

healthScenarios.label: Two circuits open
healthScenarios.detail: Recent failures have ejected the governed and private regional routes.

workloads.label: Customer support stream
workloads.detail: A standard-data conversation that needs responsive streaming.

workloads.label: EU regulated extraction
workloads.detail: Restricted documents require EU execution, strict JSON, and the highest safety tier.

workloads.label: US coding assistant
workloads.detail: A tool-enabled coding task needs streaming and a tested tool-call contract.

candidates.label: General model A
candidates.nativeNote: Native stream deltas and tool results require the North adapter.

candidates.label: Governed model B
candidates.nativeNote: Native safety blocks and JSON constraints use South-specific fields.

candidates.label: Regional model C
candidates.nativeNote: The private adapter owns its tokenizer, tool schema, and cancellation protocol.

candidates.label: Economy model D
candidates.nativeNote: This route has no streaming or tool-call contract.
